reading: Every 0-cell that belongs to a plus-shaped cross of five 0-cells (centre plus its 4 orthogonal neighbours all 0) becomes 3; overlapping crosses all fill.

new_rows.name: plus0
new_rows.datalog:
z(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 0.
pc(Y, X) :- z(Y, X), Y1 = Y - 1, z(Y1, X), Y2 = Y + 1, z(Y2, X), X1 = X - 1, z(Y, X1), X2 = X + 1, z(Y, X2).
plus0(Y, X) :- pc(Y, X).
plus0(Y2, X) :- pc(Y, X), Y2 = Y + 1.
plus0(Y2, X) :- pc(Y, X), Y2 = Y - 1.
plus0(Y, X2) :- pc(Y, X), X2 = X + 1.
plus0(Y, X2) :- pc(Y, X), X2 = X - 1.

why: exactly the cells of 0-crosses change, all to 3
invariants: all 8-cells and all 0-cells not in any cross

reading: From the single odd cell, a 1-coloured path runs down its whole column (the cell itself kept), plus a top-row run to one side corner and a bottom-row run to the opposite side corner (top-left/bottom-right when the marker row is odd, top-right/bottom-left when even).

slots.path: its full column, plus top row from that column to one side edge and bottom row from that column to the opposite side edge
slots.side: chosen by marker parity (uncertain; row odd -> top goes left)

why: path cells become 1; marker and other cells unchanged

reading: The structure touching the bottom edge is fixed; every other object falls straight down as a rigid shape (lowest first) until it would come within one empty row of the fixed structure or the bottom edge, or until it rests on an already-fallen object.

slots.subject: objects not touching the bottom border
slots.floor: objects touching the bottom border (and the bottom edge itself)
slots.stop: one background row left above the floor; direct contact allowed with other fallen objects

why: shapes unchanged, only vertical translation; each stops with exactly one empty row above the floor or touching a fallen object
invariants: colours and shapes of falling objects

reading: The one complete row is a template of two colours; each other row that shows only a short prefix is completed by copying the template pattern, recolouring template colours to the prefix's colours position by position.

slots.subject: rows with a non-empty prefix then zeros
slots.key: template colour -> prefix colour at matching positions

why: every partial row equals the template under its colour map; template and empty rows unchanged

reading: The single marker moves down one cell; then every cell above the marker's new row in columns of the same parity as the marker's column becomes 4.

new_rows.name: stripes_above
new_rows.datalog:
col(X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
col(X2) :- col(X), X2 = X + 2, px(Y, X2, C).
col(X2) :- col(X), X2 = X - 2, px(Y, X2, C).
stripes_above(Y, X) :- col(X), cell(MY, MX, MC), px(Y, X, C), Y < MY.

why: marker shifted by (+1,0); cells with row < new marker row and column parity equal to marker's become 4
invariants: cells at or below the marker's new row (except marker)

reading: The largest object is a container carrying hint cells of a shared colour; each smaller piece is pasted where its own hint cells coincide with the hints (pieces can nest inside other pasted pieces). The output is the container's box with all pieces assembled.

slots.container: largest object (its box is the output)
slots.anchor: cells of the shared hint colour/pattern in piece and container (or in an already-placed piece)
slots.placement: translate piece so its hint cells overlay the matching hint cells

why: output = container box; every piece appears unchanged at the offset where its hints match

reading: A frame of two vertical bars (different colours, 4 at their ends) is cut out; the loose two-colour shape is placed in its interior, mirrored left-right if needed so each side of the shape touches the bar of the same colour.

slots.frame: the two coloured bars with 4-end cells; its box is the output
slots.orientation: identity or horizontal flip, whichever puts each colour beside the bar of that colour
slots.place: interior between bars, rows between the 4 cells

why: output = frame box with piece filling the interior; piece colours match adjacent bar colours
invariants: piece shape up to horizontal flip

reading: Closed rings enclose holes of background; a one-cell hole is filled with 5 and a two-cell hole is filled with 7.

new_rows.name: hole1
new_rows.datalog:
z(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 0.
nfg(Y, X, count(DY, DX)) :- z(Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C).
hole1(Y, X) :- nfg(Y, X, N), N = 8.

new_rows.name: hole2
new_rows.datalog:
z(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 0.
nfg(Y, X, count(DY, DX)) :- z(Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C).
c7(Y, X) :- nfg(Y, X, N), N = 7.
hole2(Y, X) :- c7(Y, X), Y2 = Y + 1, c7(Y2, X).
hole2(Y, X) :- c7(Y, X), Y2 = Y - 1, c7(Y2, X).
hole2(Y, X) :- c7(Y, X), X2 = X + 1, c7(Y, X2).
hole2(Y, X) :- c7(Y, X), X2 = X - 1, c7(Y, X2).

why: 1-cell enclosed holes become 5, 2-cell enclosed holes become 7; nothing else changes

reading: A horizontal separator splits the grid; a column of 2s and a column of 4s appear above and below. The output is a 2x2 block of the colour whose column count grows more from the top panel to the bottom panel.

slots.panels: top and bottom halves cut by the 5-separator row
slots.measure: per colour, cell count below minus cell count above
slots.output: 2x2 grid filled with the colour of larger growth

why: output colour = argmax over {2,4} of (bottom count - top count)

reading: Each 2x2 block of 2 has four diagonal corner cells; their colours rotate one step clockwise around the block, and each corner then shoots a diagonal ray of its new colour outward away from the block to the border, crossing other rays.

slots.subject: the four diagonal corner cells of each 2x2 block of colour 2
slots.rays: from each corner, diagonally outward over background to the border (one pair shows a ray stopping early next to another block)

why: blocks unchanged; corner colours permuted clockwise; diagonal rays carry corner colours
